* clgrep-search

Lisp-aware semantic grep over .lisp/.asd/.cl/.lsp/.ros source files. 
Unlike plain text grep, returns the top-level form signature (defun/defmethod/etc.) 
containing each match. Works WITHOUT loading any Lisp system — no side effects. 
Use this first for code exploration; follow with lisp-read-file for definition detail. 
Default: returns signatures only (token-efficient). Set include_form=true for full 
form text. Set form_pattern to a shape like "(defun _ ...)" for structural matching 
(D-11: _, ?name, ... wildcards; no predicates or full unification).

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "case_insensitive": {
      "description": "Case-insensitive regex matching (default: false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "form_pattern": {
      "description": "Structural form-shape pattern (D-11 opt-in). Uses _, ?name, \n... wildcards. Example: \"(defun _ ...)\". When supplied, pattern is ignored and structural \nmatching replaces the regex fast path.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "form_types": {
      "description": "Restrict to these form types, e.g. [\"defun\", \"defmethod\"] \n(optional, all types by default).",
      "type": "array"
    },
    "include_form": {
      "description": "Include full form text in each result (default: false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "limit": {
      "description": "Maximum number of results to return (default: 200).",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Search root: absolute path or relative to project root. \nDefaults to project root.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "pattern": {
      "description": "cl-ppcre regular expression to search for (required in regex mode).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "recursive": {
      "description": "Search subdirectories recursively (default: true).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pattern"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* clhs-lookup

Look up a symbol or section in the Common Lisp HyperSpec (ANSI standard). 
Accepts a symbol name (loop, format, handler-case) or a section number (22.3, 3.1.2, 
auto-detected by the digit.dot shape) and returns the resolved entry URL plus extracted 
plain text. Reads a local HyperSpec tree; resolves nothing over the network on the 
primary path. Returns a structured not-found error when no HyperSpec is available.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "brief": {
      "description": "Return only Syntax + Arguments (compact; omits \nDescription, Examples, Notes for token efficiency).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "include_content": {
      "description": "Include extracted text content (default: true).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "query": {
      "description": "Symbol name or section number (e.g. loop, 22.3).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "query"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* code-describe

Describe a symbol: type (function/macro/class/variable/etc.), 
argument list, docstring, and source location. The attached path delegates to 
Slynk for rich arglist and description text; the hermetic path uses 
sb-introspect and cl:documentation. When the symbol is not found, returns a 
typed error with a redirect hint. Requires attached or hermetic mode.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "package": {
      "description": "Package name for unqualified symbols. \nOptional; defaults to CL-USER when omitted.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "symbol": {
      "description": "Symbol name to describe. Package-qualified form \npreferred (e.g. \"my-pkg:my-fn\"). Unqualified names use the optional package arg.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "symbol"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* code-find-references

Find all callers and references to a symbol using 
sb-introspect xref (who-calls, who-references, who-binds, who-sets, 
who-macroexpands). Returns entries with project-relative path, line, 
caller name, and relation. project_only (default true) restricts results 
to paths under the project root. relation optionally filters to one kind 
("calls", "references", "binds", "sets", "macroexpands"). 
When the symbol is not found, returns a typed error with a redirect hint. 
Requires attached or hermetic mode.

* inspect-condition

Drill into the current debugger condition at a live SLDB break: 
returns the condition's slot values and its class-precedence-list type hierarchy. 
When supplied with a result_object_id pointing to a held condition, inspects that 
object instead of the live break condition.  When not at a break (and no id given), 
returns a structured not-at-break result with condition_p=false — not an error. 
Inspecting an arbitrary captured condition that was not registered as a result 
object is a follow-on capability not yet delivered.

#+begin_src json

      "type": "string"

    "max_elements": {
      "description": "Maximum number of slots to return (default: 50).",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [],

* inspect-restart

List the live restarts at the current SLDB debugger break in 
the attached image, or invoke a chosen restart by index or name.  In attached 
mode this surfaces the restarts visible to the break thread (ABORT, CONTINUE, 
etc.) — the same menu a SLIME user sees.  Invoking a restart is state-changing: 
it unwinds the break thread's stack and resolves the break.  In hermetic mode 
there is no interactive break, so an empty restart set is returned.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "invoke": {
      "description": "0-based index of the restart to invoke.  When \nsupplied, bounds-checked against the listed restarts before the slyfun call.  \nMutually exclusive with invoke_name; invoke takes precedence.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "invoke_name": {
      "description": "Name of the restart to invoke (e.g. \"ABORT\", \n\"CONTINUE\").  Case-insensitive match against the listed restart names.  \nResolved to an index before the slyfun call.  Ignored when invoke is supplied.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "level": {
      "description": "SLDB level for the break to query or invoke against. \nDefaults to 1 (the first break level).  Must match *sly-db-level* in the break \nthread or an invoke call is silently ignored by Slynk.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* inspect-thread

Enumerate threads in the attached developer image or the 
hermetic worker process, with optional per-thread backtrace.  In attached 
mode the result reflects the live image's thread list.  In hermetic mode 
the result reflects the worker process's own threads.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "backtrace": {
      "description": "When true, the response carries an \n'eval_thread_frames' vector at the top level: a single snapshot of the \nEVAL thread's call stack (SBCL only; capped at 20 frames; empty vector on \n#-sbcl).  Frames are NOT attached per-thread because there is only one \nsnapshot — attaching the same vector to every thread entry would mislead \nthe caller about which thread the frames belong to.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "thread_id": {
      "description": "Reserved for future targeted backtrace capture. \nCurrently accepted but not used for thread selection.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* lisp-check-parens

Check balanced parentheses and reader syntax in a Lisp file or 
inline code snippet. Reports the first imbalance or reader error with 
line/column/offset. Ignores delimiters inside double-quoted strings, ; line

Provide either path (file read under sandbox) or code (inline text) — not both.

* lisp-edit-form

Structure-aware edit of a top-level Lisp form using Eclector CST parsing. 
Supports replace, insert_before, insert_after, and delete operations while preserving 
formatting and comments. PREFERRED METHOD for editing existing Lisp source code. 
Automatically repairs missing closing parentheses using parinfer (non-delete ops). 
ALWAYS use this tool instead of fs-write-file when modifying Lisp forms.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "content": {
      "description": "Full Lisp form text for replace/insert operations. \nRequired for replace/insert_before/insert_after; ignored for delete. \nMust contain exactly one top-level form. Missing closing parens are auto-repaired.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "description": "When true, return a preview without writing to disk.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "file_path": {
      "description": "Target file path (absolute, or relative to project root).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "form_name": {
      "description": "Form name to match. For defmethod include specializers, \ne.g. \"print-object ((obj my-class) stream)\". Reader macro prefixes #: and : are \nstripped automatically.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "form_type": {
      "description": "Form type to search, e.g. \"defun\", \"defmacro\", \"defmethod\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "normalize_blank_lines": {
      "description": "When true (default), normalize blank lines around top-level forms.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "operation": {
      "description": "Operation: replace, insert_before, insert_after, or delete.",
      "enum": [
        "replace",
        "insert_before",
        "insert_after",
        "delete"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "readtable": {
      "description": "Named-readtable designator for files using custom reader macros.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file_path",
    "form_type",
    "form_name",
    "operation"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* lisp-patch-form

Scoped text replacement within a matched top-level Lisp form. 
Finds old_text (exact, whitespace-sensitive) within the form identified by 
form_type and form_name, and replaces it with new_text. old_text must match 
exactly once within the form. Most token-efficient way to make small changes 
to large forms. Does NOT auto-repair parentheses — if the patch breaks form 
structure it fails immediately and no changes are written to disk. 
Use lisp-edit-form instead when replacing or inserting entire forms.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "dry_run": {
      "description": "When true, return a preview without writing to disk.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "file_path": {
      "description": "Target file path (absolute, or relative to project root).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "form_name": {
      "description": "Form name to match. Reader macro prefixes #: and : are stripped automatically.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "form_type": {
      "description": "Form type to search, e.g. \"defun\", \"defmacro\", \"defmethod\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "new_text": {
      "description": "Replacement text for old_text.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "old_text": {
      "description": "Text to find within the matched form. Exact, whitespace-sensitive. \nMust occur exactly once in the form.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "readtable": {
      "description": "Named-readtable designator for files using custom reader macros.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file_path",
    "form_type",
    "form_name",
    "old_text",
    "new_text"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

* load-system

Load an ASDF system with structured output and reload support. 
Solves three problems with using (asdf:load-system) via repl-eval: 
1. Staleness: force=true (default) clears loaded state so edits from 
lisp-edit-form become live. 2. Output noise: warnings are collected and 
returned in a structured list rather than flooding the terminal. 
3. Timeout: the load is wrapped in a real in-image timeout that actually 
interrupts a runaway compile. Requires attached or hermetic mode.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "clear_fasls": {
      "description": "Force full recompilation from source by clearing \nthe ASDF output cache before loading (default: false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "force": {
      "description": "Clear loaded state before loading to pick up \nchanges from lisp-edit-form (default: true).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "system": {
      "description": "ASDF system name (e.g. \"my-project\", \n\"my-project/tests\"). Must be findable by ASDF (registered via asdf:load-asd \nor on the ASDF source registry / Quicklisp search paths).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "timeout_seconds": {
      "description": "Timeout in seconds before the load is \ninterrupted (default: 120). The timeout fires inside the target image \nso a runaway compile is actually aborted.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "system"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* lsp-code-actions

Synthesized discover-then-apply code-actions menu for a position 
in a Lisp file. Requires a running alive-lsp server. Two-step workflow: 
(1) Call without action to DISCOVER applicable actions at line/character — 
returns a vector of action descriptors (macroexpand, remove-from-export, format). 
(2) Call with action set to one of those descriptors to APPLY it. Actions are 
backed by $/alive/macroexpand1 (macro expansion at point), 
$/alive/unexportSymbol (remove symbol from package exports), and 
textDocument/rangeFormatting (format the surrounding form). 
Returns lsp-unavailable when alive-lsp is not reachable.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "description": "Action descriptor hash-table from a prior discover \ncall. Absent for discover mode; present to apply a chosen action.",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "character": {
      "description": "0-based character offset within the line.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "file_path": {
      "description": "Absolute path to the Lisp file (within session root).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "line": {
      "description": "0-based line number of the cursor position.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file_path",
    "line",
    "character"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* lsp-diagnostics

Get compiler diagnostics from alive-lsp for a Lisp file. 
Requires a running alive-lsp server (attach-else-spawn per project root). 
Default (load=false): uses $/alive/tryCompile — safe read-only compilation 
check, does not evaluate or load the file. Optional load=true: uses 
$/alive/compile — evaluates and loads the file into the alive-lsp image 
(mutating, use with caution). Returns {messages: [{severity, location, 
message}]} where severity is 'error', 'warning', or 'info'. An empty 
messages list does not guarantee clean compilation (some errors lack source 
locations and are silently dropped). When alive-lsp is not reachable, 
returns a degraded Eclector parse check flagged degraded:lsp-unavailable.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "file_path": {
      "description": "Absolute path to the Lisp file (within session root).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "load": {
      "description": "When true, use $/alive/compile (evaluates/loads \nthe file in the alive-lsp image — mutating). Default false uses \n$/alive/tryCompile (safe, no evaluation).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file_path"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* pool-kill-worker

Kill the hermetic worker bound to the current session. 
A replacement worker is spawned on the next tool call. In-image state 
(loaded systems, REPL definitions) is lost. Use this to recover from a 
stuck or corrupted worker. Only available in hermetic mode.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "reset": {
      "description": "When true, also clears the session circuit breaker state \nso the next call can spawn without waiting for the 60-second cool-down.",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },

* project-scaffold

Generate a complete Lisp project skeleton under the session root. 
Emits a package-inferred-system with a mode-dispatching executable, Parachute 
test suite, build recipe, dev-boot script, dependency-preference agent docs, 
a copied REPL-development guide, and a selectable license with per-file SPDX 
headers. Returns a manifest of created files and next-step commands.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "author": {
      "description": "Author string for .asd :author. No newlines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "copyright": {
      "description": "Copyright holder for LICENSE file (defaults to author). No newlines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "description": "One-line project description for .asd and README. No newlines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "destination": {
      "description": "Relative parent directory under the session root \nwhere <name>/ is created (default: scaffolds). No leading / or .. segments.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "license": {
      "description": "SPDX license identifier (default: AGPL-3.0-or-later).",
      "enum": [
        "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
        "GPL-3.0-or-later",
        "GPL-2.0-or-later",
        "LGPL-3.0-or-later",
        "LGPL-2.1-or-later",
        "MIT",
        "BSD-2-Clause",
        "BSD-3-Clause",
        "Apache-2.0"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Project name in lisp-case (e.g. foo-lib). \nMust match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ and be 1-64 characters.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "overwrite": {
      "description": "When true, replace an existing scaffold directory. Default: false.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "year": {
      "description": "Copyright year for LICENSE (default: current year).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name"
  ],
  "type": "object"

* repl-eval

Evaluate Common Lisp forms in the attached Slynk image. 
Returns printed values, captured stdout/stderr, and structured error context 
(condition type, message, restarts, SBCL backtrace frames). 
Requires :slynk-attach / DSMR_SLYNK_ATTACH to be configured.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "code": {
      "description": "One or more top-level Common Lisp forms to evaluate.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "max_output_length": {
      "description": "Maximum characters for captured stdout/stderr output (default: 50000).",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "package": {
      "description": "Package name in which to evaluate; defaults to CL-USER.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "register_result": {
      "description": "When true (the default), registers the last form's first \nreturn value in the image-resident handle table and returns result_object_id. \nSet to false to suppress registration for hot loops or uninteresting results.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "timeout_seconds": {
      "description": "Seconds to wait for the eval's reply before returning a \nconnection error (default: 30). Raise for long-running forms such as big \ncompiles. The bound applies to the wait for the reply; the form itself is \nnot interrupted in the attached image.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "code"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src

* run-tests

Run tests for an ASDF system and return structured results with 
per-test pass/fail counts and source locations. 
Supports automatic framework detection (parachute/rove/fiveam) or explicit 
selection via the framework argument. 
By default, the test system is reloaded before running so edits from 
lisp-edit-form become live; pass reload=false to opt out. 
Returns: passed/failed/pending counts, framework name, duration_ms, and a 
failed_tests array with test_name/reason/source{file,line} per failure. 
Requires attached or hermetic mode.

#+begin_src json
{
  "properties": {
    "framework": {
      "description": "Force framework: \"parachute\", \"rove\", \"fiveam\", \nor \"auto\" (default: auto-detect from ASDF :depends-on).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reload": {
      "description": "Reload the test system before running (default: true). \nPass false to skip reload for tight hot-reload loops.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "system": {
      "description": "ASDF system name to test (e.g. \"my-project/tests\").",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "test": {
      "description": "Run only this specific test (fully qualified: \n\"package::test-name\"). Supported for Rove.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "tests": {
      "description": "Run only these specific tests (array of \n\"package::test-name\" strings). Supported for Rove.",
      "type": "array"
    },
    "timeout_seconds": {
      "description": "Timeout in seconds before the run is interrupted \n(default: 300). The timeout fires inside the target image.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "system"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
#+end_src
